item.title: Current Events - October 21, 2026
item.description:
October 21, 2026 (2026-10-21) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

International relations

  • Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war, United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war
    • United States special envoy Steve Witkoff arrives in Saint Petersburg to talk with Russian president Vladimir Putin about potentially resolving the war with Ukraine. (Reuters)
    • American military veteran Stephen James Hubbard, who was arrested by Russian authorities in 2022 during the Battle of Izium, is released from custody during the meeting between Putin and Witkoff. (AP) (BBC News)

item.title: Current Events - October 14, 2026
item.description:
October 14, 2026 (2026-10-14) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • Houthi–Saudi conflict
        • The Houthis claim to have shot down a Royal Saudi Air Force Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft over Saada Governorate, Yemen. Saudi authorities did not comment on the claim. (AFP via AA)
        • The Saudi Civil Defense reports that debris from intercepted Houthi cruise missiles injured four people, including a child, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, and damaged 15 homes. (AFP via CNA)
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • Two cargo ships, the Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride and the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged dry bulk carrier Cape Dao, sink after both are attacked by projectiles near the Strait of Hormuz while trying to navigate through what Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps called an "illegal and dangerous route." At least one crew member is killed in the attacks. (The Guardian) (Reuters)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
      • A Russian ballistic missile attack strikes a power station in the Dniprovskyi District, Kyiv, Ukraine, leaving more than 1,000 residential buildings without heating. (BBC News)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Darfur campaign
      • The Sudanese Armed Forces announces that they have re-captured the Bir Kelekel area of West Darfur, Sudan, from Rapid Support Forces, according to West Darfur state governor Bahr al-Din Adam Karama. (Radio Tamazuj) (AA)
  • Flamingo Revolution
    • Rioters attack government buildings, banks, businesses and other sites as anti-government protests erupt in Tirana, Albania. At least 23 police officers and six others are injured during the unrest, while 35 people are detained. President Bajram Begaj condemns the violence and appeals for calm across the nation. (AP)

Disasters and accidents

  • Three people are killed and four others are missing after torrential rainfall triggers widespread flooding across Istanbul, Turkey. (ABC News)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Southeast Asian haze
    • Singapore records its highest air pollution level of 2026 as one-hour PM2.5 concentrations reach about 288 micrograms per cubic metre amid haze from Indonesian wildfires. (AFP)
    • Timor-Leste suspends in-person classes nationwide from October 15 to 17 due to worsening air quality from wildfire smoke and pollutant particles across Southeast Asia. (AFP)

International relations

  • Colombia–Israel relations
    • Colombia opens an embassy in Jerusalem and restores its free trade agreement with Israel. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Nord Stream pipelines sabotage
      • The Ukrainian citizen accused of sabotaging the Nord Stream pipelines in 2022 faces trial at the Higher Regional Court in Hamburg, Germany, (DW) (UPI)
  • 2026 Delhi Jantar Mantar protests
    • A court in New Delhi, India, remands Cockroach Janta Party spokespeople Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka in custody for five days after police detained them for entering the restricted Jantar Mantar protest site. (AFP via RFI)
  • Censorship in Turkey
    • Turkish opposition-leaning and independent news channel Halk TV goes offline as it is raided by police and new administrators are appointed by the government. (BBC News)
  • Internet censorship in Mexico
    • President Claudia Sheinbaum signs a decree banning violent content on social media to protect minors under the age of 18. (Expansión)
  • Costa Rica inaugurates CACCO [es], a maximum-security prison modeled after El Salvador's CECOT mega-prison, aimed at holding 20% of the country's current prison population, as the homicide rate reached a record high in 2023. (Reuters)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Irish public sector strikes
    • Over 300,000 public sector workers in Ireland, including teachers, health workers, and other civil servants, start a general strike, the first in the country since 2009, to protest against a deadlock in pay negotiations. (Reuters)

Science and technology

  • Kekova shipwreck
    • The oldest known shipwreck in the world (c. 2700–2400 BC) is excavated in Kekova, Turkey. (CNN)

item.title: Current Events - October 07, 2026
item.description:
October 7, 2026 (2026-10-07) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • 2026 Yemen offensives
        • Houthi forces claim attacks on Abha International Airport and Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia that killed three civilians and injured 36 others since yesterday. (AFP via France 24)
    • Israeli settler violence
      • Israeli settlers launch an attack in the occupied West Bank targeting Palestinians, killing a man and wounding 16 other people. (Al Jazeera)
  • Ethiopian civil conflict
    • 2026 Ethiopian offensive
      • 2026 Eritrean invasion of Ethiopia
        • Eritrean forces are reported to have invaded Ethiopia's Tigray Region and are moving south toward Mekelle. (Addis Standard) (Al Jazeera)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Russian forces launch a massive ballistic missile and drone attack on Ukraine, killing at least 28 people, including 20 people killed at a single apartment hit by a North Korean KN-23 missile in Pryluky, Chernihiv Oblast, while hundreds more are wounded. (The Guardian)
    • Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Bulgaria halts the search for the 12 Syrian sailors missing since yesterday after a merchant ship sank after being hit by a drone strike in its waters. The perpetrators are still unknown. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)
  • Mali War
    • 2026 Mali offensives
      • The Malian Armed Forces and the Russian Africa Corps retake Kidal, which was captured by the Azawad Liberation Front five months ago, after days of airstrikes and ground operations. (Al Jazeera)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • 2026 Blue Nile campaign
      • Four women are killed in a Rapid Support Forces drone strike on homes and a mosque in Ad-Damazin, Blue Nile State, Sudan. (The Washington Post) (AP)

Business and economy

  • Guinea sets nationwide price ceilings for bottled water after a ban on single-use plastic water sachets causes shortages and higher prices, with retail packs of several bottle sizes capped at 25,000 francs (US$2.84). (AFP via France 24)
  • The Reserve Bank of India raises its benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%, its first increase since February 2023. (AFP via France 24)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
    • Hurricane Isaias
      • Tropical cyclone Isaias strengthens into a category 1 hurricane, becoming the first Atlantic hurricane of the season amidst a unusually quiet season caused by the ongoing El Niño phenomenon. (AP)
      • In the United States, Alabama governor Kay Ivey declares a state of emergency for 40 counties ahead of Isaias. (Reuters) (WVUA-CD)

Health and environment

  • Climate change in Antarctica
    • The British Antarctic Survey reports that Zavodovski Island in Antarctica has lost more than 500,000 chinstrap penguins since 2011, ending its status as the world's largest penguin colony as warming waters reduce access to Antarctic krill. (AFP via France 24)
  • Climate change in Australia, Mining in Australia
    • Australia's High Court rejects MACH Energy's appeal to expand the Mount Pleasant coal mine in New South Wales, finding that planning authorities failed to adequately consider greenhouse gas emissions from burning exported coal overseas. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • Elections in Mexico
    • Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum sanctions a constitutional amendment prohibiting Mexicans with dual citizenship from running for president or governor. (AA) (El Economista in Spanish)
  • International spillover of the 2026 French lycée protests
    • For a second consecutive day, riots occur in Liège, Belgium, following earlier student protests, prompting authorities to close the Guillemins railway station and urge local businesses to shut down. Over 100 people are arrested. (Al Jazeera) (RTBF)
  • Libor scandal
    • The Court of Appeal in London, United Kingdom, quashes the convictions of five former Barclays traders for manipulating Libor and Euribor, following a 2025 Supreme Court ruling that found legal errors had made similar convictions unsafe. (AFP)
  • School attacks in Poland
    • Nine people are injured in a mass stabbing at a high school in Ostrołęka, Poland. The suspect, a 19-year-old student, is arrested after being injured himself. (Reuters)

Science and technology

  • French chemist Henri B. Kagan from the Paris-Saclay University and Japanese organic chemist Kensō Soai from the Tokyo University of Science are jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for "the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis". (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - October 20, 2026
item.description:
October 20, 2026 (2026-10-20) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Sudanese civil war
    • Abyei border conflict
      • Amiet market massacre
        • The death toll in the market drone attack in Abyei on the border of South Sudan and Sudan yesterday rises to 220. (Sudans Post)
    • Blue Nile campaign
      • The Sudanese Army says that they have repelled an attack by the Rapid Support Forces and Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North (SPLM–N) on the Blue Nile state. (Sudan Tribune)
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
      • The Rapid Support Forces launches a drone strike on a power plant in Tendelti in Sudan's White Nile State, knocking out the main transition line connecting North Kordofan. (Sudan Tribune)

Disasters and accidents

  • At least 14 people are killed and 20 others are injured after a bus and a truck collide head-on in Natore District, Bangladesh. (Xinhua)
  • Twelve people are killed and 30 others are injured after a bus crashes into a truck near Cairo, Egypt. (Xinhua)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • Nigeria announces its first case of Ebola virus in the epidemic. (The Guardian)

International relations

  • Libya–Turkey relations
    • Libya (GNA)–Turkey maritime deal
      • Libya's eastern-based House of Representatives approves a 2019 maritime boundary agreement with Turkey and repeals two 2020 decisions that rejected the accord. (Reuters)
  • South Korea–Ukraine relations
    • South Korea withdraws additional embassy staff from Ukraine following a dispute over two captured North Korean soldiers who were transferred to South Korea. (AFP via RFI)
  • Houthi–Saudi conflict, Saudi Arabia–United Kingdom relations
    • United Kingdom says it will deploy RAF Typhoons to help Saudis defend against Houthi attacks. (BBC News) (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • 2026 European unrest
    • 17 October riots
      • Police arrest a 34-year old man for the arson attack on the Hôtel de Ville in Limoges, Haute-Vienne, France. (BBC)
  • 2022 San Antonio migrant deaths
    • A United States federal judge sentences a Guatemalan national to 30 years in prison for helping organize a 2022 migrant-smuggling operation in San Antonio, Texas, that left 53 migrants dead and 11 injured. (AFP via France 24)
  • Pakistan arrests a man for selling fake stamps in the United States that resulted in a $126 million loss to the U.S. Postal Service. (BBC News) (Dawn)

Politics and elections

  • Malaysia's Registrar of Societies [ms] deregisters the opposition coalition Perikatan Nasional, citing internal disputes and breaches of the constitution, preventing its component parties from contesting forthcoming elections under a common coalition banner. (Reuters)

Science and technology

  • Japanese space program
    • JAXA launches the Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft from the Tanegashima Space Center toward Phobos aboard an H3 rocket, aiming to collect at least 10 grams of surface material from the Martian moon and return the samples to Earth in 2031. (Reuters)
  • PHP2Shell
    • A critical vulnerability in PHP allowing for remote code execution is discovered, causing many websites to temporary go offline while a security update is pushed the following day. (NBC News)
  • Indian certificate authority eMudhra has its private keys compromised, revealing that some of them were extremely insecure single digit numerals. Major web browser developers Mozilla, Google, and Apple subequently block the certificates. (The Register)

item.title: Current Events - October 13, 2026
item.description:
October 13, 2026 (2026-10-13) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • Houthi–Saudi conflict
        • The Royal Saudi Air Force strikes a fuel depot near Sanaa, Yemen. The Houthis launch missiles upon multiple Saudi Arabian cities, including Riyadh and Dammam, in response. (BBC News) (CNN)
        • An administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco in Dhahran, Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia, is partially consumed by a fire after a Houthi missile is intercepted over the city by Saudi forces. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)
    • Hezbollah–Israel conflict, Funding of Hezbollah
      • Hezbollah spokesperson Ali Damoush announces that the group will pay up to US$14,000 in aid to families whose homes in Lebanon were destroyed or rendered uninhabitable during its war with Israel. Families in Beirut and its suburbs will receive $14,000, while those elsewhere in the country will receive $12,000. (AP)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Bulgaria–Russia relations, Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Two merchant ships are hit by unknown drones off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast, with one sinking. Eleven crew members are missing and 20 in total are rescued. Bulgarian prime minister Rumen Radev has blamed Russia and summoned its ambassador. It is the second such attack in six days. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
    • Six deaths are confirmed in Florida, United States, from Hurricane Isaias. (Fox Weather) (The Guardian)
  • 2026 Multan train derailment
    • At least seven people are killed and over 40 others are injured in a train derailment near Multan, Punjab, Pakistan. (AA) (AFP via The Straits Times)

Health and environment

  • Famine in Yemen, Water supply and sanitation in Yemen
    • The World Health Organization reports a surge in cholera cases in Yemen over the past three weeks. The country previously had a 6-year-long outbreak due to the ongoing humanitarian crisis. (AFP via Arab News)
  • Indonesian authorities release 20 protected green sea turtles back into the oceans off Bali after they were seized from an empty boat abandoned by wildlife smugglers last week. (AP)

Law and crime

  • 2024 Cornell University rape allegations
    • Cornell University in Ithaca, New York, United States, suspends all fraternity parties and social events for the remainder of the 2026–27 academic year following allegations that seven Chi Phi members drugged and gang-raped a student in 2024. (AFP) (BBC News)
  • Impeachment trial of Sara Duterte
    • Philippine prosecutors in the impeachment trial of vice president Sara Duterte drop three of the four impeachment charges in an attempt to speed up the trial. The Senate, sitting as an impeachment court, approves the move. (AP)
  • LGBTQ rights in Hungary
    • The Hungarian National Assembly passes an amendment repealing most provisions of the anti-LGBTQ child protection law that was previously passed during former prime minister Viktor Orbán's tenure in 2021. (DW)
  • Murder of Tupac Shakur
    • The Clark County District Court in Nevada, United States, sentences former Crips gang leader Duane "Keffe D" Davis to a minimum of 40 years in prison for orchestrating the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur in Las Vegas. (AFP via France 24) (DW)
  • Four people are killed and three more injured in a mass shooting at a memorial service in Katlehong, Gauteng, South Africa. (AP)
  • Three Indian nationals are killed and five others are injured in a suspected arson attack in Bochum, North Rhine-Westphalia Germany. A 41-year-old resident is arrested. (tagesschau)
  • Eight people are injured in a mass stabbing at a supermarket in Incheon, South Korea. A suspect is arrested. (BBC News) (CNA)
  • Students in Tirana, Albania, throw bricks at the Ministry of Education building, prompting riot police to respond. (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2026 World Artistic Gymnastics Championships
    • The Netherlands denies visas to Russian artistic gymnasts Anna Kalmykova, Viktoria Listunova, and Angelina Melnikova for the world championships in Rotterdam, while four other Russian gymnasts receive permission to enter the country. (AP)
  • In auto racing, Formula 1 announces a new grand prix in Kigali, Rwanda, to run for at least 10 years starting in the early 2030s with a new track. This would be the first F1 grand prix in Africa since South Africa in 1993. (AP)

item.title: Current Events - October 15, 2026
item.description:
October 15, 2026 (2026-10-15) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Yemeni civil war
    • Houthi–Saudi conflict
      • Saudi Arabia says that it has intercepted a missile intended for Medina. However, the Houthis denied launching a missile at the city. (The Hill) (France 24)
    • The Houthis launch missiles against Al-Maashiq Palace, headquarters of the Presidential Leadership Council and official residence of President Rashad al-Alimi, in Aden, Yemen, killing five people and injuring 16. No member of the council is harmed in the attack. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)

Business and economy

  • China–North Korea relations
    • The New Yalu River Bridge connecting Dandong, China, and Sinuiju, North Korea, opens following a 12-year delay. (BBC News) (NK News)
  • The European Central Bank authorizes UniCredit to raise its stake in Commerzbank above 30% without an upper limit, allowing the Italian bank to proceed toward taking control of the German lender. (The Eastern Herald)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Peshawar school roof collapse
    • A roof collapses at a school in Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, killing 34 students and a teacher, and injuring 50 more people. (BBC News)
  • 2026 Indonesia wildfires
    • Four people are killed fighting wildfires in Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park in East Java, Indonesia, after flames and thick smoke trapped them. Two others suffer serious burns. (AFP)
  • Seven people are missing after a San Marino-flagged tanker catches fire off the coast of Romania amid recent drone attacks on merchant shipping in the Black Sea. Search and rescue operations are underway to locate the missing crew members. (Politico)

Health and environment

  • The United Kingdom declares a severe drought in Cornwall, Devon, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex, and West Sussex after prolonged low rainfall left more than 80% of England in drought and major reservoirs below 20% capacity. (AFP)

International relations

  • Germany–Iran relations, Antisemitism in 21st-century Germany, Iranian external operations
    • A court in Hamburg, Germany, sentences a Danish national to eight years and six months in prison and an Afghan national to four years and six months in prison for plotting to assassinate Josef Schuster, the president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, on behalf of Iran. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Silver Rail Elementary School shooting
    • Three children and a teacher are killed in a mass school shooting at the Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, United States. Two other people are wounded. The perpetrator, a 16-year-old male, is shot and killed by a bystander. (AP) (The Guardian)
  • Capital punishment in the United States
    • U.S. president Donald Trump announces that the Department of Defense has reversed its plan to livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan, the perpetrator of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting, scheduled for December 3. (AFP via France 24) (AP)
  • Argentine police arrest at least 25 people after clashes during a university funding protest in Buenos Aires, while eight police officers are injured. (AFP via France 24)
  • Northern Irish politician and former Democratic Unionist Party leader Jeffrey Donaldson is sentenced to 15 years in prison for child sexual abuse and rape. The offences occurred between 1985 and 2008. (AP) (BBC News)

Science and technology

  • Astronomers discover the first green star, WD J1330+6435, according to a study published by RAS Techniques and Instruments. (Popular Science)
  • At the General Conference on Weights and Measures, the International Bureau of Weights and Measures votes to abolish future leap seconds and make Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) continuous, starting 20 May 2027. To account for future differences between UTC and International Atomic Time, a leap hour will be observed as needed. (The Guardian) (Scientific American)

Sports

  • 2026 Major League Baseball season
    • In baseball, the Milwaukee Brewers sweep the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS to advance to the 2026 World Series, their first since 1982. (ESPN)

item.title: Current Events - October 08, 2026
item.description:
October 8, 2026 (2026-10-08) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 United States military buildup in the Middle East
        • The USS Abraham Lincoln returns to San Diego, California, U.S., at the North Island Naval Air Station following its nearly seven-month deployment in the Middle East. (The Guardian) (Los Angeles Times)
      • U.S. president Donald Trump says that the U.S. military will not attack Iran before the midterm elections next month. (AP)
    • Gaza war
      • Gaza war hostage crisis
        • The Israel Defense Forces announce that they have killed Muhammad Muhsen Nimr Yazji, a Hamas militant who took part in holding Emily Damari, Romi Gonen, and Matan Angrest during an airstrike in Gaza City. (The Jerusalem Post)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Russian forces launch a ballistic missile attack on two buses in the city of Kramatorsk in Ukraine, killing at least 30 people, while 18 others are wounded. (Al Jazeera)
  • Mexican drug war
    • Ten inmates are killed and 16 more injured during a prison riot in Mazatlán, Sinaloa, Mexico. (AP)

Arts and culture

  • 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
    • Canadian poet Anne Carson is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for "her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms ‌for contemporary literature". (BBC News)
  • The Bank of England announces that the Atlantic puffin, barn owl, buff-tailed bumblebee, and European hedgehog will feature on the next set of pound sterling notes to be issued in the United Kingdom. It will be the first time animals have replaced people on banknotes in England, which is intended to increase awareness of British wildlife. (BBC News)

Business and economy

  • AI boom, Semiconductor industry in Taiwan
    • The Taiwanese finance ministry reports that exports reached a record US$87.2 billion in September, while imports rose to a record $63.6 billion and the trade surplus reached a record $23.6 billion, citing demand for artificial intelligence-related hardware. (AFP) (Reuters)
  • The Hungarian newspaper Népszabadság, which was shut down in 2016 during the government of former prime minister Viktor Orbán, relaunches as an online news site. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
    • Hurricane Isaias
      • In the United States, Georgia governor Brian Kemp declares a state of emergency ahead of Hurricane Isaias. (Fox 5 Atlanta)
      • Hurricane Isaias strengthens into a category 2 Atlantic hurricane. (AP)
  • Severe rainfall in Chile, particularly in Santiago, caused flooding, river overflowing, mudslides, and power outages, killing one person, injuring six others and damaging over 2,000 homes. (NBC News)

International relations

  • South Korea–Ukraine relations, North Korean involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war
    • South Korea recalls its ambassador to Ukraine after accusing Ukraine of breaching a non-disclosure agreement by disclosing the transfer of two captured North Korean soldiers to South Korea. (AFP via The Straits Times)

Law and crime

  • 2009 Fort Hood shooting, Capital punishment in the United States
    • United States secretary of defense Pete Hegseth announces the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan, the perpetrator of the 2009 Fort Hood shooting, will be publicly broadcast. (AFP via RFI) (CNN)
  • 2026 Poland school stabbings
    • A 15-year-old student carries out a mass stabbing against staff members at a primary school in the village of Leszczydół-Nowiny, Wyszków County, Poland, killing one person and injuring two more. The suspect is taken into police custody. (Reuters)
  • Relationship of Prince Andrew and Jeffrey Epstein
    • High Court judge Nicholas Hilliard of England and Wales quashes search warrants used on Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes, finding errors in Thames Valley Police's applications and issuing judge Mark Lucraft's consideration of legally protected material. (AP)

Politics and elections

  • Next Guinea-Bissau general election
    • The Government of Guinea-Bissau announces that presidential and parliamentary elections scheduled for December 6 will be delayed. (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2026 Nippon Professional Baseball season
    • In baseball, Teruaki Satō of the Hanshin Tigers wins the Triple Crown. (Kyodo News)
  • 2026 WNBA season
    • In women's basketball, Las Vegas Aces center A'ja Wilson wins a record fifth WNBA Most Valuable Player, becoming the first player in league history to win the award for three years in a row. (ESPN)
  • Swiss and Sunderland A.F.C. footballer Granit Xhaka receives a two-year probation after admitting to obtaining a fake COVID-19 vaccination certificate during the COVID-19 pandemic. (ESPN)

item.title: Current Events - October 18, 2026
item.description:
October 18, 2026 (2026-10-18) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
      • Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reports that an oil tanker has caught on fire and exploded in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz after striking a naval mine. (Middle East Eye)
  • Haitian conflict
    • El Salvador–Haiti relations
      • Armed gang members ambush Salvadoran Air Force personnel serving with Haiti's Gang Suppression Force in Port-au-Prince, using gunfire and explosives. Four Salvadoran service members remain missing after escaping their burning armored vehicle. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • A truck loses control and runs over devotees outside a temple in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, India, killing at least 13 and injuring nearly 40 others. (AFP via Dawn) (The Indian Express)
  • At least eight people are killed and eight others are injured after a mortar shell explosion in Zawiya, Libya. (Xinhua)
  • A light aircraft crashes into a dry riverbed in Kondariotissa, Pieria, Greece. Two people are killed. (Xinhua)

Health and environment

  • Equatorial Guinea announces that it will expand its program combating malaria to the mainland and Annobón. The program has already heavily reduced malaria cases on Bioko Island. (The Independent)

International relations

  • Cross-strait relations
    • The Taiwanese coast guard drives away 16 Chinese coast guard, research, and fishing vessels operating near Taiwan and the Pratas Island, including some that entered restricted waters. (AFP via The Hindu)
  • Free trade agreements of Vietnam
    • Vietnam signs a free trade agreement with the European Free Trade Association (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland) that reduces or eliminates tariffs on industrial, agricultural, and fish products and covers services, intellectual property, and sustainable development. (AFP)

Politics and elections

  • Water scarcity in Mexico
    • Protests continue for the second week in Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico, over water shortages and widespread contamination. A study in June found that at least 93% of households' water systems contained no residual chlorine, but had elevated levels of lead, mercury, nitrates, and E. coli. (Reuters) (Türkiye)
  • The Iranian parliament appoints Mehrdad Akhlaghi as Minister of Defence, replacing acting minister Majid Ebn-e-Reza. (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - October 11, 2026
item.description:
October 11, 2026 (2026-10-11) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • Houthi–Saudi conflict
        • October 2026 attacks on Saudi Arabia airports
          • Houthis launch an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, causing a fire, killing one person and injuring multiple people. (Sky News) (Al Jazeera)
          • An Indian national injured in yesterday's attack on King Khalid International Airport dies from his injuries, raising the total death toll to 13. (Reuters)
        • The Royal Saudi Air Force launches an airstrike in Sanaa, Yemen, killing a child and wounding seven other people. (Al Jazeera)
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • A drone strikes the Nicaragua-flagged tanker MT Petro Dolphin near Sohar, Oman, leaving two Indian sailors missing and prompting the rescue of nine others. Omani authorities conduct search-and-rescue operations for the missing crew members. (AFP via Arab News)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
      • Airstrikes are launched at the Egypt–Sudan border targeting an artisanal gold mine in a mountainous area, killing at least 72 people. (Sky News)
  • Mexican drug war
    • Three civilians and two police officers are killed in a mass shooting in Jacona, Michoacán, Mexico, while six other people are wounded. Separately, three gunmen are killed in a shootout with police in Zamora. (OEM in Spanish)
  • Colombian conflict
    • Four FARC dissidents are killed and 12 rifles seized after an airstrike by the National Army of Colombia against a guerrilla camp in Norte de Santander Department, Colombia. (El Tiempo in Spanish)
    • A drone strike kills a soldier in La Vega, Cauca Department, Colombia. (Publimetro in Spanish)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Budhi Gandaki flood
    • Ten people are reported missing and at least 35 houses and six bridges are swept away in a major flash flood in Gorkha District, Gandaki Province, Nepal. The exact number of casualties is unknown. (ANI via Gulf News) (Nepal Views)
  • At least 139 people are killed, 84 more are missing, and over 80 are rescued when a boat carrying migrants shipwrecks off the coast of Djibouti. (AFP via France 24)
  • Eleven people are killed and 27 others are injured when a tour bus collides with a truck at a toll road of Otoyol 5 in Akhisar, Manisa Province, Turkey. (Türkiye Today)
  • One person is killed and around 19 others are injured, including four critically, when a passenger bus plunges down a slope and crashes into a residential complex in Valparaíso, Chile. (Teletrece in Spanish)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • The Kenyan health ministry reports that no Ebola cases have been reported since one patient died from the disease on October 5, with 293 tests conducted. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Indonesia wildfires
    • The Indonesian forestry ministry and International Animal Rescue release eight orangutans rescued from wildfires into a protected wildforest in West Kalimantan after fires destroyed habitat near plantations. (AFP)

Law and crime

  • 2026 anti-CEC protests
    • An executive magistrate's court in New Delhi, India, orders the release of Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other leaders, requiring them to avoid breaches of the peace for one year after their detention. (AFP via France 24)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Kraków mayoral election
    • Independent candidate Łukasz Gibała wins the Kraków mayoral election in Poland against government-backed Civic Platform senator Monika Piątkowska. (Politico) (Euronews)
  • 2026 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa state of emergency
    • Pakistani president Asif Ali Zardari declares a state of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and suspends its provincial government amid disputes over the province's response to Islamist militancy. (AFP via RFI)
  • 2027 French presidential election
    • Raphaël Glucksmann is elected as a candidate in the 2027 French presidential election during the Socialist Party primary, receiving more than 66% of the votes in the first round. (AFP via RFI)

item.title: Current Events - October 17, 2026
item.description:
October 17, 2026 (2026-10-17) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • Egypt–Saudi Arabia relations, Houthi–Saudi conflict
        • Egyptian president Abdel Fattah El-Sisi states that Egypt will take all necessary steps to protect and defend Saudi Arabia should the latter so desire. (AFP via Arab News)
    • Gaza war
      • Israeli settler violence
        • Masked Israeli settlers attack a group of European diplomats, including the Belgian consul general, French and Polish diplomats, and Catholic representatives visiting Taybeh in the occupied West Bank, Palestine. (AP)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Kolkata Durga Puja crowd crush
    • At least 17 people are killed and 25 others are injured in a crowd crush at a pandal in Kolkata, West Bengal, India. (Hindustan Times) (Sky News)
  • CFB Wainwright fire
    • An explosion and wildfire occurs at the CFB Wainwright, a Canadian Armed Forces base in Alberta. Four people are killed and dozens more injured. (CBC News) (CTV News)
  • Ten tourists are killed and nine others sustain injuries after a resort catches fire in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh. (AA)
  • Eight people are killed and eight others are injured after a minibus carrying 23 passengers plunges into a drain along the Delhi–Mumbai Expressway near Kota, Rajasthan, India. (The Times of India)
  • A Piper Tomahawk II aircraft crashes near Drymen, Stirling, Scotland, killing the two people on board. (BBC News)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • Kenya confirms four additional cases of Bundibugyo ebolavirus, including three health workers who treated Kenya's first patient and one of his relatives, raising the national total to seven. All four are already in quarantine. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • 2026 European unrest
    • 2026 French student protests
      • 17 October riots
        • Over 500,000 people take part in protests across France, according to the national trade union confederation, while clashes and riots erupt in large cities. (FranceInfo)
        • Protesters force their way into Marseille's town hall and vandalize the interior before being dispersed. (CNews)
        • In Lille, protesters storm the city hall and damage the premises prior to being removed by security forces. (Ouest-France)
        • Dozens of shops are looted across major French cities amid widespread rioting and civil unrest. (BFMTV)
      • The Hôtel de Ville in Limoges is partially destroyed by fire. (Le Parisien in French)
    • 2026 French fuel protests
      • Yellow vests activists hold mass demonstrations across France against rising fuel prices and join the student protests. (Al Jazeera)
  • 2026 anti-CEC protests
    • A court in New Delhi, India, orders the release of Cockroach Janta Party founder and activist Abhijeet Dipke on a peace bond, one day after police detained him while he was heading to a protest against the Election Commission of India. (AFP via France 24)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Czech Senate election
    • In Czechia, opposition parties win 22 of the contested 27 seats in the Senate. The lead party of prime minister Andrej Babiš's government, ANO 2011, comes in third place. The election is the first time in the country's history where governing parties did not win a single seat in a senatorial election. (AP)
  • Protests against Donald Trump
    • The fourth round of No Kings protests are held across the United States against president Donald Trump and his administration and to encourage early voting ahead of the upcoming midterm elections. (AFP) (USA Today)

Sports

  • 2026–27 NHL season
    • In ice hockey, the Florida Panthers become the first team in the National Hockey League to record a natural hat trick in three consecutive games. (The Athletic via The New York Times)

item.title: Current Events - October 10, 2026
item.description:
October 10, 2026 (2026-10-10) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Ethiopian civil conflict
    • 2026 Ethiopian offensive
      • 2026 Eritrean incursion into Ethiopia
        • Ethiopian forces regain control of Adigrat in the Tigray Region following a withdrawal of Eritrean forces. Celebrations are reported in the city following the withdrawal. (Oman Observer) (Al Jazeera) (UA News)
  • Yemeni civil war
    • Houthi–Saudi conflict
      • October 2026 King Khalid International Airport attack
        • Twelve people are killed and 309 more injured in a Houthi missile attack against Terminal 3 of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. (The Wall Street Journal) (Reuters)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Zaporizhzhia strikes
      • At least 20 people are killed and 18 others are injured in a Russian airstrike on a five-story residential building in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine. (Ukrainska Pravda)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
    • The National Hurricane Center reports that Hurricane Isaias has weakened to a post-tropical cyclone after making landfall near Destin, Florida, United States. (WVTM-TV) (NBC News)
    • Four people are killed during Isaias' landfall in the United States, with two deaths in Escambia County, Florida, and another two in Alabama. (The Guardian)
  • 2026 Pacific hurricane season
    • Tropical storm Simon strengthens into a category 4 Pacific hurricane with 150 mph (240 kph) winds as it heads towards Mexico's coast. (AP) (The Rio Times)
  • A man is killed after jumping into a tiger enclosure and being attacked at Yorkshire Wildlife Park in South Yorkshire, England. The tiger was uninjured. (BBC News)

Law and crime

  • Censorship in India
    • 2026 anti-CEC protests
      • Indian authorities are placing New Delhi under a security lockdown and have been detaining thousands of demonstrators to block a rally organized by the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party. (BBC News) (The Guardian) (The New York Times)
  • 2026 Poland school stabbings
    • A woman carries out a mass stabbing at an adult school in Warsaw, Poland, injuring three people. The suspect is arrested. It is the third such attack in the country in a week. (AP)

Sports

  • 2026–27 La Liga
    • In association football, the match between Rayo Vallecano and Athletic Bilbao is abandoned by referee José María Sánchez Martínez due to fans throwing objects at the pitch to protest against Rayo president Raúl Martín Presa. (Reuters)
  • 2026 NCAA Division I FBS football season
    • In American college football, the Kentucky Wildcats football team defeats the LSU Tigers 35–34 on a 2-point conversion in overtime, becoming the first team in FBS history to win consecutive overtime games by one point since overtime was introduced in 1996. (The Athletic via The New York Times) (The Score)
  • 2026 Il Lombardia
    • In cycling, French cyclist Paul Seixas wins the 120th edition of the Giro di Lombardia in Italy, becoming the youngest person to do so. (NBC Sports) (The Guardian)

item.title: Current Events - October 19, 2026
item.description:
October 19, 2026 (2026-10-19) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Sudanese civil war
    • Abyei border conflict
      • Amiet market massacre
        • A drone strike kills at least 73 people at a market in the disputed Abyei area between South Sudan and Sudan. (Reuters)
    • Rapid Support Forces atrocities in Khartoum
      • Three children are killed in an alleged Rapid Support Forces drone strike in Khartoum, Sudan. (AP)
  • Yemeni civil war
    • 2026 Yemen offensives
      • 2026 Shabwah missile attack
        • A missile attack by the Houthis kills 58 soldiers and injure over 200 at a training center in Shabwah Governorate, Yemen. There are 14 missing. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • Mediterranean Sea migrant smuggling
    • Twelve migrants, including an infant, are killed when two separate speedboats capsize off the coast of the Lesbos and Samos islands in Greece. (AP)
  • Fourteen miners are killed and seven more injured when an open pit gold mine collapses in Nariño Department, Colombia. (AP)

International relations

  • Andorra–European Union relations, San Marino–European Union relations, Potential enlargement of the European Union
    • Andorra and San Marino each sign an association agreement with the European Union. (The Brussels Times)
  • Gaza Strip famine, Palestine and the United Nations
    • The World Food Programme cuts monthly food aid for about 500,000 people in the Gaza Strip because of funding shortages, reducing the number of recipients from 1.6 million to 1.1 million. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • Cuba–United States relations
    • 1996 shootdown of Brothers to the Rescue aircraft, United States embargo against Cuba
      • A judge in Miami-Dade County, Florida, United States, issues a no-bail bond arrest warrant for former Cuban president Raúl Castro after Florida attorney general James Uthmeier charged Castro with conspiracy to commit first-degree murder by directing spies to infiltrate Brothers to the Rescue and ordering the attack on their planes in 1996. (Al Jazeera)
  • Israeli settler violence
    • Israel Police arrest 10 people in the occupied West Bank over attacks on American photojournalist Heidi Levine and the mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries, France, who were travelling with European diplomats, and seize vehicles and other evidence during raids. (AFP via France 24) (Reuters)
  • Shakahola Forest incident
    • A Kenyan court convicts Good News International Ministries leader Paul Nthenge Mackenzie of murdering 190 children and an adult whose deaths were linked to starvation in Shakahola Forest. (Reuters)
  • Independent Australian MP Helen Haines is deliberately hit by a car outside her office in Wangaratta, Victoria. Police arrest the car's driver, while Haines is airlifted to a hospital. Haines later had both her legs amputated. (AFP) (The Guardian) (Reuters)
  • A teacher and a student are injured in a stabbing attack at a school in Bistrița, Romania. The 13-year-old suspect is arrested. (Reuters)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Alberta referendums, 2026 Alberta independence referendum
    • Albertans vote on ten referendums, including one to decide if Alberta should seek separation from Canada. (Reuters)
    • Albertan voters reject pursuing a future independence referendum, with more than three-quarters supporting the province remaining in Canada. (BBC News)

item.title: Current Events - October 12, 2026
item.description:
October 12, 2026 (2026-10-12) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Yemeni civil war
    • Houthi–Saudi conflict
      • October 2026 attacks on Saudi Arabia airports
        • The Houthis claim to have attacked King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, with a ballistic missile for a third consecutive day. (Reuters)
        • Delta Air Lines postpones direct flights from Atlanta's Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International Airport to Riyadh following attacks by the Houthis on the country. (The Hill)
  • Kivu conflict
    • M23 campaign
      • Former Congolese president Joseph Kabila announces the formation of a rebel political-military coalition named Front for the Refoundation of the Nation, which includes the March 23 Movement, Twirwaneho and the Congo River Alliance. The group, led by Kabila, says it aimed to coordinate "resistance forces" to topple the Government of President Félix Tshisekedi. (BBC)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Nobel Prizes
    • American economists Robert Ernest Hall and Michael Dean Woodford are jointly awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for their work on "microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation". (CNN)
  • American visual images company Getty Images announces that it will file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Pacific hurricane season
    • Two deaths are reported after hurricanes Rachel and Simon made landfall on Mexico's coast, with Guerrero governor Evelyn Salgado and Baja California governor Marina del Pilar Ávila confirming their deaths. (Al Jazeera)
  • Incidents at Six Flags parks
    • One person is killed and four others are injured after an accident on the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia in Mableton, Georgia, United States. (BNO News)
  • A fire destroys the historic Marché des Enfants-Rouges food market in Paris, France. (France 24)

International relations

  • International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Russia–European Union relations
    • The Council of the European Union approves the 22nd package of sanctions against Russia, targeting 1,569 individuals and entities of the country's military and industrial complex. (EU Council)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Aubagne school shooting
    • A 14-year-old student opens fire at a middle school in Aubagne, France, injuring two staff members, before being detained. (AP) (France 24)
  • 2026 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa state of emergency
    • Pakistan's federal government detains hundreds of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) members, including former Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi and other provincial officials, after suspending the PTI-led provincial administration and imposing emergency rule. (AFP via RFI)
  • 2026 French supermarket cyber attack
    • A cyber attack without attribution against French supermarkets results in losses worth millions of euros. (BBC News)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Estonian presidential election
    • Ülle Madise, who was elected by the Riigikogu in September, takes office as President of Estonia, succeeding Alar Karis. (Estonian World)

Science and technology

  • Generative AI chatbot Character.ai files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, citing costs and litigations including those linked to teen suicides. (The Wall Street Journal) (CBS News)

item.title: Current Events - October 16, 2026
item.description:
October 16, 2026 (2026-10-16) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Sudanese civil war
    • Thirty people are killed and 47 people are injured in a drone strike on a cattle market in Nyala, South Darfur, Sudan. (AFP via Dawn)
  • Israeli settler violence
    • Israeli settlers attack and beat a group of Palestinians and an American journalist from The Washington Post. (The Times of Israel)

Health and environment

  • Deforestation of the Amazon rainforest
    • Brazilian environment minister João Paulo Capobianco [pt] reports that deforestation in Brazil's Amazon rainforest fell to 5,796 km2 (2,238 sq mi) in the year through July 2026, the lowest level since 1988 except for 2012. (AFP via France 24)

International relations

  • Australia–Fiji relations
    • Australia agrees to provide Fiji with solar-, wind-, and wave-powered Bluebottle maritime drones and training for surveillance and efforts against drug trafficking and other transnational crime, with deployment expected in 2027. (AFP via RFI)
  • Hungary–Ukraine relations, Accession of Ukraine to the European Union
    • Hungarian prime minister Péter Magyar and Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy agree to improve bilateral relations during a meeting in Brussels, Belgium, with Hungary lifting objections to further European Union accession talks for Ukraine following progress on ethnic Hungarian minority rights in Ukraine. (Reuters)

Law and crimes

  • 2026 anti-CEC protests
    • Cockroach Janta Party leader Abhijeet Dipke is detained in Delhi, India, ahead of the party's planned march. (BBC News)
  • South African police rescue about 200 people from an unregistered rehabilitation centre in Mpumalanga and arrest two people while investigating alleged kidnapping and health and safety violations. Fourteen people receive medical treatment following the rescue. (Reuters)
  • A judge in Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico, sentences three Mexican men to over 158 years in prison each for the murder of two Australians and an American in 2024. (AP)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Moroccan general election
    • Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, who was named Prime Minister by King Mohammed VI on 29 September, takes office as her four-party coalition Government is formally appointed. (Morocco World News)
  • 2026 Czech Senate election
    • Czechs begin voting in the second round to elect 22 senators who were not elected in the first round. (Romea)

Sports

  • 2026 WXV Global Series
    • In women's rugby union, Canada defeats England 24–21 in a WXV Global Series match in Toronto, ending the Red Roses' four-year unbeaten run at 41 matches (the longest in rugby union history) after Shoshanah Seumanutafa scores a late try. (Stuff)

item.title: Current Events - October 09, 2026
item.description:
October 9, 2026 (2026-10-09) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • 2026 Iran war
    • Casualties of the 2026 Iran war
      • The Pentagon raises the U.S. military death toll in the Iran war to 21 after reporting two noncombat deaths. (The Hill)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war, 2026 Blue Nile campaign
      • An RSF drone strike in Blue Nile State, Sudan, kills 41 displaced people. (AP)

Disasters and accidents

  • Tropical cyclones in 2026
    • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
      • Hurricane Isaias
        • Isaias strengthens into a category 3 Atlantic hurricane. It would later weaken to category 2, with 365,000 people in Alabama and Florida, United States, reported to be without power ahead of its landfall. (AP) (MS Now)
        • Isaias makes landfall near Destin, Florida, and weakens to a category 1 hurricane. (AP) (Reuters via The Straits Times)
    • 2026 Pacific hurricane season
      • Hurricane Rachel
        • Flooding is reported in areas of Southern California, U.S., including Long Beach and Newport Beach, and the National Hurricane Center issues a tropical storm warning for the area. The warning is the first issued for San Diego County, California, since 2023 during Hurricane Hilary. (Los Angeles Times) (KTLA) (KNSD)
      • Hurricane Simon
        • Simon strengthens into a category 2 Pacific hurricane. (AP)
  • 2026 Panama earthquake
    • A magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes Herrera Province, Panama. A nationwide tsunami warning is issued. (Reuters) (USA Today)
  • A passenger bus collides with a truck on a road in Mkambarani, Morogoro Region, Tanzania, and catches fire, killing 28 people. (AP)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
    • Eight more children in Bangladesh are reported to be killed from measles, bringing the death toll past 1,155. (BSS)

International relations

  • Montenegro–Russia relations
    • Montenegro expels Russian military blogger Mikhail Zvinchuk and four other Russian nationals on national security grounds after detaining them in Risan. (AFP via RFI)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Musée Renoir theft
    • Six people suspected of stealing Pierre-Auguste Renoir's paintings Young Woman at the Well and Madame Colonna Romano from the Musée Renoir in Cagnes-sur-Mer, Alpes-Maritimes, France, are arrested, and the artworks are recovered. (AP) (Reuters)
  • 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
    • South African judge and former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Navi Pillay is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for "her efforts to promote peace and international law". (DW)
  • Shootings by U.S. immigration agents in the second Trump administration
    • Clashes erupt in New York City, United States, between protestors and police after the shooting of a Dominican Republic national with a criminal conviction by ICE agents. The man, who was in a car alongside a child, was then detained while being wounded. (Al Jazeera)
  • 2026 Erie shooting
    • Eight people are killed, including the perpetrator, in a mass shooting at a home in Erie, Pennsylvania, United States. (AP) (BBC News)
  • The Supreme Federal Court of Brazil issues an arrest warrant for Eduardo Bolsonaro, the brother of presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, on charges of lobbying the U.S. to interfere in the trial of his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro. (Al Jazeera)
  • A man armed with a knife takes 13 children and staff members hostage at a school in Curitiba, Paraná, Brazil, and threatens to set it on fire, before being shot dead by police. The hostages are rescued, with two children sustaining injuries. (AP)

Politics and elections

  • Next Palestinian legislative election
    • Palestinian vice president Hussein al-Sheikh announces that the Palestinian legislative election planned for November 28 will be postponed, possibly until September 2027, along with the also delayed presidential election, because of worsening conditions throughout Palestine. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Czech Senate election, 2026 Czech municipal elections
    • Czechs begin voting in the first round to elect one-third of the Senate. Incumbent prime minister Andrej Babiš seeks gains of his coalition in the Senate. Municipal elections are also underway. (AP)
  • The Mauritanian government of Prime Minister Moctar Ould Diay resigns over power outages. However, President Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani reappoints Diay, asking him to form a new government. (AFP via Arab News)
  • Pope Leo XIV approves Filipino cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle's election as dean of the College of Cardinals, making him the first Asian to lead the body that elects a new pope. (Reuters)
